defs.title: Holding Site Order
defs.author: Cordon Quarantine Authority
defs.body:
CORDON QUARANTINE AUTHORITY - DESIGNATED HOLDING SITE
EMBER CREEK HOT SPRINGS (PRIVATE RESORT)

This property is requisitioned as a holding site for persons found within the quarantine zone without a registration card.
Persons held here will remain on the property until cleared by a medical officer. Exterior doors will be secured. Food and water will be delivered by road every third day.
The proprietor will provide lodging and heat. Persons showing fever, eye discharge or white growth on the skin will be separated from the others and reported to the duty soldier.
Attempting to leave the property is a violation of the quarantine order.

Under it in pencil, a column of dates. The deliveries stop after the second one.

defs.title: Letter on the Bed
defs.author: June Marsh, cabin 4
defs.body:
Dear Mum,
We were only meant to stop one night. The man at the road block said the springs were safe and warm and they'd clear us in a day. That was eleven days ago. They nailed the front of the bathhouse and we come and go by the side door like staff.
Everyone sits in the hot water all day because there is nothing else to do and it is the only place that is warm. Mrs Vail says the heat cooks the sickness out. I do not think it does. The steam room has a white fur on the benches now and nobody will go in except Mr Pruitt from cabin 3, and he sits in there for hours.
The soldier on the desk has the cough. I am going to try the trail over the ridge tonight with the Haddad boy. If this reaches you, I tried. June

defs.title: Note Under the Key Ring
defs.author: Walt Ober, caretaker
defs.body:
Connie -
I am done carrying for you. The pump room key is here on my ring, the padlock on the door is the only thing keeping folks off the valves, and if you want the plunge kept hot you can go down and turn them yourself. Emil has your spare. He won't come up out of that cellar anymore, says the boiler needs him and the heat keeps the white off him. It doesn't. I saw his hands.
Cabin 2 and cabin 3 are sick. I put the Pruitts in 3 and shut the door on them. Don't let the kid out, he bites.
I'm going to sit a while in the rock pool where it's quiet. - W.

defs.title: Boiler and Water Log
defs.author: Emil Haugen, bath attendant
defs.body:
Spring at the cistern 61 C. Plunge 41. Steam room 52 and wet.
Mrs V says keep it all hot, the Cordon doctor told her heat kills it. Doctor has not come.
Day 6. Bloom on the steam room benches, white like frost. Scrubbed it with lye. Back by evening.
Day 9. Bloom in the cistern room, on the pipes. It likes the warm. It likes the wet. We are giving it the best house in the valley.
Day 13. The soldier on the desk is sick. Mrs V has locked herself in the suite and sent her spare key down for me to keep, she says I am the only one she trusts. I keep it in my shirt.
Day 16. Coal nearly gone. Hands stiff. It is very warm down here and I am very tired. If I sleep, the key is on me.

defs.title: Constance Vail's Diary
defs.author: Constance Vail, proprietor
defs.body:
Sixty years my family has kept this water, and now soldiers tell me who may leave my own front door. They nailed it shut themselves. I gave them the key to the side door and they gave me a paper.
The guests are frightened. I told them the truth as I know it: heat and minerals, that is what people came here for, to be cured. Keep the plunge at forty, keep the steam room hot, keep everyone in the water.
The steam room is wrong. It glows in the dark now. Emil says it is only a fungus. Walt will not go near it.
I have the strongbox and the deeds up here and I have bolted the door. The spare is with Emil, safe in the cellar where nobody goes. I hear them on the gallery at night, walking round and round the pool. I keep the shotgun on the door.
